# Social media for nonprofits: 6 engagement tips

![avatar](https://pro.gofundme.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/cropped-profile-pic-for-author-blurb-50x50.png)

By [Rosa Hernandez](https://pro.gofundme.com/c/blog-author/rosagofundme-com/)

![A group of friends taking a selfie](https://pro.gofundme.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/blog_Social-Media-for-Nonprofits-6-Tips_v3_1836x918-1224x612.jpg)

Published: October 22, 2026 • Reading Time: 7 minutes

[](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https://pro.gofundme.com/c/blog/nonprofit-social-media-engagement-tactics/&t=Social+media+for+nonprofits%3A+6+engagement+tips)[](http://linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://pro.gofundme.com/c/blog/nonprofit-social-media-engagement-tactics/&title=Social+media+for+nonprofits%3A+6+engagement+tips)[](http://twitter.com/share?text=Social+media+for+nonprofits%3A+6+engagement+tips&url=https://pro.gofundme.com/c/blog/nonprofit-social-media-engagement-tactics/)[](https://mail.google.com/mail/?view=cm&to=&su=Social+media+for+nonprofits%3A+6+engagement+tips&body=https://pro.gofundme.com/c/blog/nonprofit-social-media-engagement-tactics/)

Picture this: a community member searches for cause-related hashtags on Instagram and finds your nonprofit. A supporter shares your message on Facebook and encourages their network to donate. A company finds your LinkedIn profile while researching [sponsorship opportunities](https://pro.gofundme.com/blog/creative-examples-corporate-sponsorships/).

These are just a few examples of the powerful role social media can play in your conversion funnel, from when a potential donor first learns about your nonprofit organization to their initial gift and ongoing support. Social media platforms are a valuable tool for increasing awareness of your cause and engaging people with your organization’s mission, whether you run a large charity or a small grassroots nonprofit.

In fact, GoFundMe’s [Kindness Gap report](https://pro.gofundme.com/c/resources/the-kindness-gap) shared that every organic social channel we measured brings in more first-time donors to GoFundMe Pro than organic search, paid search, or paid social.

Below, we offer six tips for how nonprofits can leverage their social media strategy to guide potential supporters from awareness to engagement to conversion. We also cover how to choose the right platforms for your organization and how GoFundMe Pro can make your social media plan easier with new [nonprofit social-sharing tools](https://pro.gofundme.com/platform/meta-social-sharing/).

## 6 social media engagement tips for nonprofits

In [_The Social State of Giving_](https://www.gofundme.com/c/socialgiving), GoFundMe’s report on how social media impacts giving, we found that every time an organizer shares their fundraiser online, it can help drive an additional $100 toward their goal.

Gen Z seems particularly enthusiastic about this, **with 46% saying they believe people should share their donations online to help spread the word and inspire others**. Half also said that they share causes or fundraisers with their social networks at least once a week.

Knowing which social media marketing strategies work can help nonprofits better meet supporters where they are. Here are six to get you started.

### 1\. Lean into videos

Videos remain some of the most engaging content on social media. Current [Instagram benchmark data](https://www.socialinsider.io/social-media-benchmarks/instagram) shows Reels earning meaningfully higher engagement than static image posts, though carousels have recently edged ahead of Reels as the platform’s single top-performing format. Meanwhile, the video-focused platform TikTok has by far the [highest engagement rate](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1274133/engagement-rate-per-post-social-media/) per post: 3.7% in 2025, compared to 0.48% for Instagram and 0.15% for Facebook.

To remain relevant in the feed, nonprofits should [make more videos](https://pro.gofundme.com/blog/11-nonprofit-videos-that-inform-and-inspire/), including livestreams. However, it’s critical to note that it’s not always professionally produced video content that sees the most engagement. Quick, relatable video snippets can capture your target audience’s attention without requiring significant time or budget to create.

### 2\. Keep using hashtags

If you’ve used social media for a while, hashtags may seem outdated. However, data still shows that they can increase engagement. Depending on the account size, using hashtags in an Instagram post can [raise reach by 36%](https://www.searchlogistics.com/learn/statistics/hashtags-statistics/) for smaller accounts, whereas posts on X (formerly Twitter) that use hashtags see about twice the engagement of those that don’t.

It’s clear that social media users still follow and participate in hashtag campaigns, providing nonprofits with an opportunity to boost key initiatives to new audiences. We’ll share more details on the most popular and effective hashtags to use based on the social media platform below.

### 3\. Work with the limits of static posts

Static posts, such as a [solo image](https://www.socialinsider.io/blog/instagram-benchmarks/) on Instagram or a [link-only post](https://buffer.com/resources/best-time-to-post-on-facebook/) on Facebook, perform the lowest of any social media format. This doesn’t mean you shouldn’t use these post types, but consider ways to boost their potential engagement.

On Instagram, use the carousel feature to add up to 20 images within a single post that users can scroll through. **Carousel posts see greater engagement because they show up in users’ feeds twice: your first photo will be their initial impression, and when they refresh their feed, they’ll then see the second photo in your lineup.**

Remember that visual content tends to receive the most engagement. If sharing a link on Facebook, try sharing it with a photo. You can use a service like Bitly or TinyURL to shorten links and make your posts look cleaner.

You can also optimize engagement for static posts by using a mix of infographics, photos, stories, and appeals, and engaging with your audience in the comments.

# Social media for nonprofits: 14 expert-backed tips for success

Anyone who uses social media for nonprofits knows there are unique challenges. Get your message out and start fundraising with these tips.

[Sam Lauron](https://blog.hootsuite.com/author/sam-lauron/) October 23, 2025 16 min read

 ![cover image](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Social-media-for-nonprofits-14-expert-backed-tips-for-success-556x556.png)

## Table of Contents

[The benefits of social media for nonprofits](https://blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-for-nonprofits/#The_benefits_of_social_media_for_nonprofits)

[14 expert-backed social media strategy tips for nonprofits, according to the experts](https://blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-for-nonprofits/#14_expert-backed_social_media_strategy_tips_for_nonprofits_according_to_the_experts)

[Free social media template just for nonprofits](https://blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-for-nonprofits/#Free_social_media_template_just_for_nonprofits)

[3 best social media tools for nonprofits](https://blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-for-nonprofits/#3_best_social_media_tools_for_nonprofits)

[FAQs about social media for nonprofits](https://blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-for-nonprofits/#FAQs_about_social_media_for_nonprofits)

Nonprofit organizations do great things to make the world a better place — and often on a shoestring budget. Driving awareness to your cause is typically one of the most critical (yet challenging!) parts of the job, and social media is a great place to get the word out.

Social media for nonprofits is different from most industries because the stakes are high. Goals include, but are not limited to, growing your donor base, recruiting volunteers, and sharing your impact. No small feats!

However, with a little education, a social media strategy, and the right tools, any nonprofit social media account can reach its maximum potential. Keep reading, and we’ll show you how.

### Key Takeaways

1.  **Social media helps nonprofits do more with less.** Even with tight budgets, the right strategy can grow your audience, attract donors, and bring your mission to life.
2.  **Authenticity builds trust and engagement.** Nonprofits that share real stories, impact updates, and behind-the-scenes moments connect more deeply with their communities.
3.  **Strategy beats spontaneity.** A clear plan — from knowing your audience to choosing the right platforms — helps you stay consistent and make the most of every post.
4.  **Tools and teamwork make it scalable.** Social media management platforms like Hootsuite (and creative tools like Canva) help small teams save time, stay organized, and turn awareness into action.

## **The benefits of social media for nonprofits**

There are [5.17 billion social media users](https://blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-statistics/#Global_social_media_usage_statistics) in the world, a number that’s only growing each year.

But people aren’t just on social media to connect with friends. In fact, Americans [spend over five hours a week](https://preply.com/en/blog/what-americans-learn-on-social-media/) learning on social media.

If you want to spread the word about your cause, social media is a great place to post about your cause and give people something new to learn about.

Here are some other ways to use social media for your nonprofit:

*   Drum up donors (who keep coming back)
*   Recruit qualified volunteers
*   Connect with clients of your programs
*   Create an engaged community of supporters
*   Get your important issues in front of the right audience
*   [Ask for donations on social media](https://blog.hootsuite.com/examples-of-how-to-ask-for-donations-on-social-media/)

Let’s go over some of these benefits in more detail, along with real-life examples of nonprofits using social media.

### **Promote awareness to your cause**

Social media is an easy, effective way to spread the word about your organization’s mission.

People can’t get behind you if they don’t know what you’re all about, right? Drum up support for your cause with regular reminders of what you do and who you help.

[Bat Conservation International](https://www.batcon.org/), for instance, often shares Facebook posts that inform audiences about how the nonprofit works with bat habitats — while also educating people about different bat species.

 ![A close-up of a person holding a bat, with a cave in the background, promoting bat conservation efforts as an example of social media for nonprofits.](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Social-media-for-nonprofits-1-620x606.png)

_Source:_ [_Bat Conservation International_](https://www.facebook.com/BatCon)

### **Drive fundraising efforts**

[Social media is a natural fit](https://blog.hootsuite.com/examples-of-how-to-ask-for-donations-on-social-media/) for your next fundraising drive. Include donation links in your posts or Stories, and pop one right into your social media bio, too, to make it super easy for anyone to help fund your cause.

Whether you’re promoting a specific fundraising campaign or encouraging people to contribute regularly, followers can donate in just a few clicks.

According to [Katherine Bruchalski](https://www.linkedin.com/in/katherine-bruchalski-a1a513153), Digital Media Manager at [EarthDay.Org](http://earthday.org/), social media also offers nontraditional ways to fundraise.

“While this might not be the first tool you think of for nonprofits, Instagram’s shopping features can actually help with fundraising too,” says Bruchalski.

“By integrating things like merchandise or donation campaigns directly into the platform, you can boost awareness and drive donations as social commerce continues to grow.”

### **Connect with your clients**

Being accessible to clients and donors is important for any nonprofit. If someone has questions about your services or is eager to make a significant donation, you’re going to want them to be able to reach you.

By operating a social media account (or accounts), you’re creating multiple avenues for connection. And increasingly, social media is the [preferred communication tool](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/operations/our-insights/social-media-as-a-service-differentiator-how-to-win).
